summary: The Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) Foreign Postgraduate Scholarship pays for a Master's degree at an overseas university for indigenes of the nine Niger Delta states. NDDC describes it as covering tuition plus grants for accommodation, air travel, monthly living costs and study materials, with amounts set by the exchange rate at payment time. Winners hold a strong first degree (2:1 or First), already have a foreign admission letter in one of eight listed fields, and then score highly in a computer-based test (CBT) and an oral interview.
lookfor: Proof you are from the Niger Delta: a Local Government identification letter, later checked with your LGA and Community Development Committee
A First Class or Second Class Upper degree in a relevant field (the 2026 advert asked for this; some reports say 2:2 — check the current advert)
An unconditional or conditional postgraduate admission letter from a recognised overseas university in one of the eight listed disciplines
A high CBT score: reporting on the 2026 round says about 70% was needed to move forward
A clear, confident oral interview: why this course, why this university, and how you will serve the Niger Delta
cycle: The 2026/27 round opened 23 March 2026 and closed 19 April 2026; the CBT and oral interviews ran in Port Harcourt in May 2026. The next round is not yet announced — if it follows the last two years, expect an advert around March–April 2027, so get your overseas admission letter before then.

eligibility.q: Are you an indigene of Abia, Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Cross River, Delta, Edo, Imo, Ondo or Rivers State, and can your Local Government issue an identification letter?
eligibility.no: This award is only for Niger Delta indigenes. Look at your own state scholarship board, the PTDF Overseas Scholarship, or international awards such as Chevening and Commonwealth.

eligibility.q: Will you be under 40 years old when you apply?
eligibility.no: The 2026 advert excluded applicants aged 40 or above. Consider awards without an age cap, e.g. university-funded scholarships abroad.

eligibility.q: Do you have a First Class or Second Class Upper bachelor's degree?
eligibility.no: The 2026 advert asked for a First or 2:1. If you have a 2:2, check the next advert closely; otherwise consider awards that accept a 2:2 plus work experience.

eligibility.q: Is your intended Master's in Agricultural Sciences/Biotechnology, Engineering, Environmental Sciences, Geosciences, IT/Artificial Intelligence, Medical Sciences, Architecture/Building Technology or Law?
eligibility.no: Only these eight fields were funded in 2026. Choose a course that clearly fits one of them, or use a different scholarship.

eligibility.q: Have you completed NYSC (discharge certificate) or been officially exempted?
eligibility.no: Finish NYSC first or get your exemption letter. You cannot upload a call-up letter instead.

eligibility.q: Can you get a postgraduate admission letter from an overseas university before the NDDC deadline?
eligibility.no: Start applying to universities abroad now (October–January). Without the admission letter you cannot apply.

eligibility.q: Are you applying for a Master's (not a PhD)?
eligibility.no: The 2026 foreign round was for Master's only. For a PhD, look at TETFund (if you are a lecturer), PTDF, Commonwealth or university-funded PhD studentships.

steps.title: Confirm you fit every NDDC rule
steps.why: Thousands apply (about 12,000–16,000 in 2026) and the first cut is a paper check. One missing rule means automatic rejection.
do: Read the eligibility questions above and answer each one honestly.
Check your state of origin and Local Government Area (LGA) on your birth certificate or certificate of origin.
Calculate your age on the likely closing date (around April 2027).
Check your degree class on your certificate or statement of result.
Write down which of the eight NDDC disciplines your planned Master's fits.
tips: If your course could fit two fields (e.g. environmental engineering), pick the one your admission letter title matches best.
avoid: Assuming 'Niger Delta region' means living in Port Harcourt. It is about your state of origin and LGA letter.
check: I meet every rule above
I know which discipline my course falls under

links.t: Channels TV guide to the 2026/2027 round

steps.title: Understand how winners are picked
steps.why: Selection is a funnel: paper check, CBT, oral interview, then LGA/community verification. Knowing this lets you prepare early for each gate.
do: Note the stages: online application → preliminary shortlist (WAEC/NECO result, degree class, LGA letter) → CBT → oral interview → LGA and Community Development Committee verification.
Note the numbers: in 2026 about 12,277 applied, 5,986 passed the CBT and 2,492 reached interviews. In 2025 about 200 awards were made.
Read NDDC's own news report on the 2026 interviews.
Decide on a backup scholarship in case you are not selected (e.g. Chevening, Commonwealth, university awards).
tips: Treat NDDC as one of several applications, not your only plan.
avoid: Paying anyone who promises to 'fix' your selection. NDDC says scores appear instantly and are not changed.
check: I can name all four selection stages
I have at least one backup award

links.t: NDDC news: Foreign Scholarship — transparency and fairness (May 2026)
The Sun: 6,200 applicants take NDDC CBT

steps.title: Build your timeline backwards from April
steps.why: The NDDC window has been only about four weeks long. Everything slow (admission, LGA letter, NYSC certificate) must be done before it opens.
do: Put 'NDDC window likely opens ~March 2027' in your calendar, then set reminders every week from February to check nddc.gov.ng.
Set a target: overseas admission letter in hand by end of February 2027.
Set a target: LGA identification letter collected by January 2027.
List the universities you will apply to and each one's application deadline.
tips: Follow NDDC's verified social media for the advert, but always confirm on nddc.gov.ng.
avoid: Waiting for the advert before applying to universities. You need the admission letter to apply.
check: My calendar has all target dates
I know where the advert will appear

steps.title: Choose your course and overseas universities
steps.why: Your admission letter decides your field and country, and NDDC does not allow changes of course or institution later.
do: Shortlist 3–5 one-year or two-year Master's courses that match one NDDC discipline.
For each, note the entry grade, English test rule, fee, start date and application deadline.
Prefer universities that issue decisions quickly (many UK universities decide in 2–6 weeks).
Check that the course is full-time and on campus (not online).
tips: Pick a course you can explain in one sentence linked to a Niger Delta problem (oil-spill clean-up, flooding, health, agriculture, digital jobs).
avoid: Choosing a course outside the eight fields because it sounds attractive.
Planning to defer: NDDC said deferment is not permitted.
check: Every course on my list fits an NDDC discipline
I know each application deadline

links.t: YouTube: choosing a UK Master's as a Nigerian

steps.title: Write your statement of purpose for the universities
steps.why: You cannot apply to NDDC without an admission, and the statement of purpose is the main thing a university reads after your grades.
do: Open each university's application page and copy its exact personal statement question and length limit.
Paragraph 1: the problem you want to solve and why it matters in the Niger Delta.
Paragraph 2: your degree, final-year project and best grades that prepared you.
Paragraph 3: work, NYSC or volunteering experience that shows skill.
Paragraph 4: why this course and this university (name 2 modules or staff).
Paragraph 5: your plan after graduation and how it helps your community.
tips: Reuse the core story for the NDDC interview later — it will make your answers consistent.
avoid: Copying online samples; universities use plagiarism checkers.
Long life stories with no link to the course.
check: Each statement names the specific course
It fits the university's length limit

links.t: YouTube: how to write a statement of purpose

steps.prompt: Each university sets its own question — usually: why this course, what prepared you, and your career plan.
steps.limit: Set by each university (often 500–1,000 words or about 4,000 characters) — check each one

steps.title: Get transcripts and degree certificate
steps.why: Universities abroad need transcripts to admit you, and NDDC needs your degree certificate to confirm your class.
do: Go to your university's Academic Affairs / Exams and Records office (many now use an online transcript portal).
Request an official transcript sent to each foreign university, plus one student copy for yourself.
Pay the fee and keep the receipt; note the reference number.
Collect your degree certificate, or a signed statement of result if the certificate is not ready.
Scan everything in colour as PDF.
tips: Ask early: Nigerian transcript requests can take several weeks.
avoid: Uploading blurry phone photos of documents.
check: I have clear PDFs of my certificate and transcript
Transcripts are on their way to my universities

steps.title: Book an English test if your university asks
steps.time: 4–8 weeks to prepare and get results
steps.why: Without meeting the English rule you may only get a conditional offer, and NDDC does not pay English test fees.
do: Check each university: some accept a WAEC/NECO English credit or a 'medium of instruction' letter from your Nigerian university instead of IELTS.
If a test is needed, book IELTS Academic, TOEFL or PTE at an official centre and budget for the fee in naira.
Practise with free official materials for 3–4 weeks before the test.
Send scores to your universities as soon as they arrive.
tips: Ask the admissions office by email whether they waive IELTS for Nigerian graduates — many UK universities do.
avoid: Booking the test so late that your admission letter is still conditional when NDDC opens.
check: I know each university's English rule
My test (if needed) is booked

steps.title: Ask two referees for university references
steps.why: Universities need references to admit you. NDDC itself did not ask for references in 2026, but some reports mention a guarantor's letter of good conduct — check the advert.
do: Choose two lecturers who know your work (project supervisor first); a work supervisor can be a third.
Send each a short email: the courses, deadlines, your CV, transcript and draft statement.
Enter their official email addresses in each university portal.
Remind them politely one week before each deadline.
tips: Use your referees' official university emails, not Gmail, where possible.
avoid: Asking referees at the last minute.
check: Both referees agreed and have my documents

steps.title: Submit university applications and secure an admission letter
steps.why: The admission letter is your entry ticket to NDDC. No letter, no application.
do: Submit 3–5 applications on the universities' own websites.
Track each in a table: submitted date, reference number, decision.
Answer any requests for missing documents within 48 hours.
When an offer arrives, download the official offer letter as PDF.
If the offer is conditional, work to meet the conditions quickly.
tips: Accept the offer that best fits an NDDC discipline, and keep the others until NDDC results are out.
avoid: Paying large tuition deposits before you know your funding, unless you can afford to lose them.
check: I have at least one admission letter as a PDF

links.t: Watch: NDDC Scholarship Application 2026 (step by step) (Opportunity place)

steps.title: Get your LGA letter, NYSC certificate and photo ready
steps.why: The LGA letter is how NDDC confirms you are from the Niger Delta, and it is checked again with your community at the end.
do: Visit your Local Government secretariat and request a Local Government identification letter (some call it a certificate of origin). Bring your birth certificate and a parent's or community leader's confirmation if asked.
Find your NYSC discharge or exemption certificate and scan it.
Find your WAEC/NECO result — the preliminary shortlist checks it.
Take a recent passport photograph on a plain background and save it as JPG.
Put all files in one folder named clearly (e.g. Surname_LGAletter.pdf).
tips: Ask the LGA office for the letter on letterhead, signed and stamped, and keep the original safe for later verification.
avoid: Using an old or unsigned LGA letter.
Uploading an NYSC call-up letter instead of the discharge certificate.
check: I have: LGA letter, degree certificate, NYSC certificate, admission letter, WAEC/NECO, photo

steps.title: Fill and submit the NDDC online form
steps.why: The portal gets heavy traffic near the deadline. Applying early avoids crashes and missed uploads.
do: When the advert appears on nddc.gov.ng, follow its link to the NDDC scholarship portal (scholarship.nddc.gov.ng was used in 2026).
Create your account with your own email and phone number.
Fill personal details exactly as on your certificates.
Upload each document in the right box.
Submit. A registration number is assigned automatically — print or save the acknowledgement page.
Write your registration number in a safe place.
tips: Apply in the first week of the window.
Use a laptop and a stable connection.
avoid: Using any website not linked from nddc.gov.ng.
Paying anyone for 'application forms' — the application is online.
check: I have my registration number and printed acknowledgement

links.t: NDDC official website (start here for the portal link)
Opportunity Desk summary of the 2026 advert

steps.title: Prepare for the computer-based test (CBT)
steps.why: The CBT cut most candidates in 2026: about 6,000 of 12,000+ passed. Reports say around 70% was needed.
do: Watch nddc.gov.ng and your email for the CBT shortlist, date and venue (Port Harcourt in 2026).
Practise timed aptitude questions daily: verbal reasoning, numeracy, general knowledge and current affairs on Nigeria and the Niger Delta.
Revise basic facts about NDDC: its mandate and the nine member states.
Plan travel and arrive early with your acknowledgement slip and ID.
tips: Practise on a computer, not a phone, so you are used to the format.
avoid: Believing anyone who sells 'leaked CBT questions'.
check: I have done at least five timed practice tests

links.t: YouTube: aptitude test practice for Nigerian CBTs

steps.title: Prepare for the oral interview
steps.why: The interview score helps set the final cut-off. In 2026 about 2,500 were interviewed for roughly 200 places.
do: Write 1-minute answers to: Tell us about yourself. Why this course? Why this university? How will this help the Niger Delta? What will you do after graduating?
Practise aloud with a friend who asks follow-up questions.
Bring originals of every uploaded document, neatly arranged in a folder.
Dress formally and arrive early.
tips: Give one concrete local example (e.g. a specific community problem) — panels remember specifics.
check: I can answer the five core questions without notes
My originals are ready

links.t: YouTube: scholarship interview questions and answers

steps.title: Pass verification, then plan your money carefully
steps.why: Final selection includes checks with your LGA and community. Past NDDC scholars have also suffered long payment delays, so you need a backup plan.
do: Make sure your LGA and community leaders can confirm you when contacted.
When awarded, read the award letter fully: what is covered, when money is paid, your obligations.
Ask your university about payment plans in case NDDC funds arrive late.
Keep some savings or a family backup for your first months abroad.
Apply for your student visa as soon as your university and NDDC paperwork allow.
tips: Keep copies of every NDDC letter and email; universities may ask for proof of sponsorship.
avoid: Resigning your job or travelling before written confirmation of funding.
check: I have a written award letter
I have a backup for late payments

faq.q: Can I apply before I have an admission letter?
faq.a: No. In 2026 a postgraduate admission letter from an overseas university was a required upload.
The 2026 foreign round was for Master's degrees only. NDDC has also announced a separate local postgraduate scheme for Nigerian universities — watch nddc.gov.ng.

faq.q: Which countries can I study in?
faq.a: The advert says a recognised overseas university; it does not list countries. Past scholars studied in the UK, Europe and America.
The 2026 adverts did not mention a fee. Be very careful with anyone asking for payment.

faq.q: Can I change my course or defer?
faq.a: No. NDDC said deferment, change of institution and change of course are not permitted.
NDDC has not published a fixed figure; amounts depend on the naira exchange rate at payment time.
